description: Branch names, and the OCI tags they publish to (paper Section 7.5). A branch is a named pointer; on a registry it is a tag, and the mapping is fixed by the protocol so that a branch one client publishes is a branch to every other client that lists the repository. Two kinds of case: a name, with the tag it maps to or the reason it is refused, and a tag, with the branch it names or null when it names none. Both directions are published because each is a separate place to disagree: an implementation that maps names correctly and reads tags back loosely would list another runtime's release tags, or its signature fallback tags, as branches.

grammar.name: One or more segments separated by '/'. Each segment is [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]*. No '.', so the mapping is reversible.
grammar.tag: The default branch, named 'main', publishes to the deployment's default tag. Every other branch publishes to 'br.' followed by the name with each '/' replaced by '.'. The tag is at most 128 characters, as OCI requires.
grammar.reading: A tag names the default branch when it equals the deployment's default tag. Otherwise it names a branch when it begins with 'br.' and the remainder, with each '.' replaced by '/', is a valid name other than 'main'. Every other tag names no branch.

vectors.name: default_branch
vectors.note: The branch every brain has, publishing where it always did. A brain with no ref table is on it.

vectors.name: default_branch_follows_the_deployment
vectors.note: The default branch publishes to whatever tag the deployment treats as current, not to a fixed word. Only the br. prefix is fixed by the protocol.

vectors.name: one_segment
vectors.note: The prefix, then the name. Underscores and hyphens are carried as they are.

vectors.name: two_segments
vectors.note: The slash an OCI tag cannot carry becomes a dot. Names carry no dots, so the dot is never ambiguous on the way back.

vectors.name: three_segments
vectors.note: Every slash is replaced, not only the first.

vectors.name: mixed_case
vectors.note: Case is preserved, because OCI tags are case-sensitive and a mapping that folded case would make two branches publish to one tag.

vectors.name: longest_name
vectors.note: A 125-character name maps to a 128-character tag, the longest OCI allows. Present so that an implementation with an off-by-one bound has something to fail against.

vectors.name: name_one_too_long
vectors.reason: its tag would exceed the 128 characters OCI allows
vectors.note: One character past the boundary. Refused at creation, because a branch that cannot be published is a branch nobody else will ever see.

vectors.name: empty
vectors.reason: a name has at least one segment
vectors.note: Nothing to publish under.

vectors.name: dot_in_a_segment
vectors.note: The rule that keeps the mapping reversible. a.b would publish to br.a.b, the tag a/b already owns.

vectors.name: leading_hyphen
vectors.reason: a segment begins with a letter or digit
vectors.note: Would read as a flag on every command line that takes a branch.

vectors.name: empty_segment
vectors.note: Two slashes would become two dots, which no valid name produces, so the tag could not be read back.

vectors.name: trailing_slash
vectors.note: The empty segment at the end.

vectors.name: leading_slash
vectors.note: The empty segment at the start.

vectors.name: non_ascii
vectors.reason: segments are ASCII letters, digits, '_' and '-'
vectors.note: OCI tags are ASCII. A name that cannot become a tag cannot be published.

vectors.name: whitespace
vectors.reason: segments are ASCII letters, digits, '_' and '-'
vectors.note: Neither a tag nor something a shell passes intact.

vectors.name: the_default_tag
vectors.note: The deployment's current tag names the default branch.

vectors.name: the_default_tag_elsewhere
vectors.note: Under another deployment default, that tag is main's instead.

vectors.name: latest_under_another_default
vectors.note: latest is not special. Where the deployment publishes main to stable, latest is a release tag like any other.

vectors.name: a_branch_tag
vectors.note: The mapping read back: drop the prefix, dots become slashes.

vectors.name: a_release_tag
vectors.note: A tag without the prefix names no branch. Releases and branches share a repository without colliding.

vectors.name: prefix_main
vectors.note: Decodes to main, which is the default branch's name and never a br. tag. Read as a branch it would let anyone publish a second, competing main.

vectors.name: prefix_alone
vectors.note: Decodes to the empty name, which is not a name.

vectors.name: double_dot
vectors.note: Decodes to a//b, which no valid name produces.

vectors.name: hyphen_first
vectors.note: Decodes to -x, which is refused as a name, so the tag is not a branch.

vectors.name: referrers_fallback_tag
vectors.note: The tag a registry without the Referrers API uses for signatures. It shares the repository with branches and must never be listed as one.
